recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Body: Kyle and Serena Denton are community herbalists creating wild-crafted and organic plant medicines out of Milwaukee since 2015. These products work—not in the allopathic "pharma-medicine" way, but in a terrain-support, consciousness bolstering plant-teacher sort of way.

recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.
recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Name: The Sonic Slider

His supplements are formulated with a focus on bioavailability, so the body can actually absorb and use what you're taking rather than letting it pass through unused. It's a simple, no-nonsense approach to filling the nutritional gaps most modern diets leave behind.

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Listening to the land before you build", "body": "Topher Gardner opens with the practice he brings to every site, walking a property with copper dowsing rods and letting the ground answer. He describes finding three water lines and a nexus point on a client's Missouri land, where a dragon path crosses a ley line and the rods spin for everyone who holds them. Chance Garton connects it to his own dowsing work reading a client's chakras and energy field. The shared claim is that the body and the landscape run on the same currents, so the same simple tool reads both if you quiet your intention and actually listen."}, {"title": "Telluric currents, diamagnetism and poltergeists", "body": "Much of the early hour is vocabulary. Topher defines telluric current as bioelectricity running horizontally through the ground, and magnetic current as what the geology itself carries, citing Walter Russell's line that magnetism is the daughter of electricity. Missouri, he says, is intensely diamagnetic because of its solid rock and enormous aquifers, unlike the mush under Florida or Michigan. Where the two currents cross, he says, you get the nexus points associated with UFOs, plasma balls and poltergeists. Chance floats piezoelectricity in the crystalline bedrock as the mechanism, referencing Greg Little's quartz in a bathtub lighting up the water."}, {"title": "Domes, corners and Victor Schauberger", "body": "Topher fell into building by accident, broke in Central America in 2007, sensitive to the tin roofs he says block the sushumna. Reading The Hand Sculpted House sent him to earth building, and domes won him over for reasons both practical and energetic. A dome has no vertices, so it is easy to clean and spiders will not web it, while a 1967 cube bedroom collects what he and Crow call angles of sorrow. He ties it to Victor Schauberger's flow forms, where curves keep air, water and energy moving so nothing stagnates in a corner."}, {"title": "The house as a capacitor", "body": "The title idea arrives mid build. Laying superadobe bags for a beehive dome, Topher realized the fifteen hundred meters of barbed wire tying the concentric rings together was effectively one enormous coil, insulated by earth held inside polypropylene. Ground potential at the base and, by his figure, eighteen hundred volts at the top made him see the structure as an earth battery, and homes as things that should power themselves. His plan is to route conductive orgonite channels into a mojo cell, a Joe cell variant of nested cylinders holding structured water between an anode and a cathode."}, {"title": "Water, orgone and new water", "body": "The last stretch turns to Wilhelm Reich, whose microscope let him watch living samples without killing them, and whose book Murder of Christ Topher credits with pulling him out of ashram passivity. Reich coined orgone from the orgasm as a collapse of the field, which Chance renames the ingasm. Topher claims his one liter accumulator pours out a liter and a half, water arriving in real time. Following Kenneth Wheeler and Walter Russell, he argues ether condenses into light, light into hydrogen, and that temperature is not heat but the rate of potential change."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Renaissance Construction-Wizard Topher Gardner returns to InnerVerse to share his vision for a new era of bio-energetically enhanced home building techniques. Home is where the hearth is, and should be a place that supports ultimate rejuvenation and rest, yet most modern abodes are little more than paper-mâché EMF-microwaves. Tune in to learn about building orgone-accumulating structures that are restorative to all environmental dimensions, within and without.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: The Plus+ Extension is epic, as we discuss using biochar to build EMF-shielded structures, Topher unveils details about his ultimate build strategy, we gain more insight about how our field and the environment are signaling to each other, and we take a peek behind the fourth wall at the existence of reality's author.
